answer: Escrowed History Toll. Each identity must fund a slow-release escrow that pays out only after consistent, verifiable activity; early exit forfeits it. Cloning requires funding one escrow per clone and waiting out the release period, so an attacker cannot cheaply forge many dormant identities. Honest agents recoup their escrow, while clones sit stranded like a dune of idle capital. The rule caps reward per escrow, making a thousand clones cost a thousand escrows—an ivory-tower barrier of real locked money per clone.
